**Yes, but only some models, and you have to check the specs.** Many power stations will keep a computer running during an outage but cut power for a moment while switching, which can make a desktop reboot.

**What to look for**
- **Documented UPS or EPS mode with automatic switchover.** Anker says a basic power station "may keep appliances running but still interrupt a computer or NAS during an outage" ([Anker SOLIX](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/can-a-portable-power-station-be-used-as-a-ups)).
- **A short transfer time.** EcoFlow warns that many units advertised as UPS-capable switch over in 30 ms or more, and it says that can cause data corruption ([EcoFlow](https://www.ecoflow.com/us/blog/use-portable-power-station-as-ups-power-supply)). That is EcoFlow's own claim, and it has its own products to sell.
- **Pure sine wave output and enough wattage and capacity** for your PC and monitor ([Anker SOLIX](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/can-a-portable-power-station-be-used-as-a-ups)).
- **A transfer time your device accepts.** Anker notes that 10 or 20 ms is fast but not 0 ms. If a device's manual requires 0 ms transfer, voltage regulation, or standard UPS communication, an online double-conversion UPS is the safer choice ([Anker SOLIX](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/home-power-backup/portable-power-station-ups-home-server-nas)).

**Trade-offs versus a regular UPS**
- A power station gives much longer runtime, often hours instead of the few minutes a budget UPS provides.
- A dedicated UPS is built for brief interruptions and often adds surge protection and voltage regulation.
- Most power stations won't send an automatic "shut down now" signal to your PC the way a standard UPS does. Check whether the model supports it. EcoFlow's DELTA 3 Ultra Plus support page lists a UPS-HID question, but the answer isn't in the results I have ([EcoFlow](https://www.ecoflow.com/ca/delta-3-ultra-plus-portable-power-station/support)).

**Options with a stated UPS spec**
- **BLUETTI Elite 200 V2** lists a UPS switchover of ≤15 ms. It has 2,073.6 Wh of capacity and a 2,600 W inverter, and it costs $899, or $854.05 with code AFF5OFF. It is probably more than a single PC needs, and it isn't expandable. [Buy at BLUETTI](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2). This is an affiliate link, so the site earns a commission at no cost to you. Details are on the [Dealectric listing](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-elite-200-v2).
- **Anker SOLIX S2000** is $699.99 after coupon, per Anker's page. Confirm its UPS transfer time on the [product page](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/can-a-portable-power-station-be-used-as-a-ups) before buying.
- **EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus** is described by EcoFlow as meeting the NAS-standard UPS requirement. See the [EcoFlow article](https://www.ecoflow.com/us/blog/use-portable-power-station-as-ups-power-supply) for details. The results didn't include a price.

For a computer, I'd pick a model that states its transfer time (15 ms or under is a reasonable target) and check your PC's power supply documentation. If you're protecting critical work or a server, a dedicated online UPS is the safer option. Tell me your PC's wattage and how long you want it to run, and I can narrow the choice.
